record.title: Hilsa restriction on Indian pilgrimage travel and observed restoration by July 2025
record.scope: Hilsa–Purang route for Indian pilgrimage travellers
record.exceptions: Other cohorts or traffic are not established as restricted; see current phase qualification.
record.enforcement: Source-specific reported interruption and scoped restoration; see Chronology phases.
record.relationship: No matching Hilsa Indian-pilgrim parent in the baseline. SA021 is Nepal’s national human-movement rule; SA027 concerns India–China border trade at different passes. Passage already reported for Humla in 2023 concerns a different or broader eligible cohort.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no inference of current border status.
record.current_timing: dated evidence; numeric duration withheld; see qualification
record.current_corrections: This is an Indian-pilgrim restriction and restoration through Hilsa, not closure of all Hilsa traffic. Actual pilgrimage passage is evidenced by July 2, 2025. Mid-March arrivals at Simikot airport and June permission language are not exact border-crossing dates. Other Humla traffic was reported open in 2023. No five-year numerical operational duration is assigned.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the Indian pilgrimage-travel interruption and reported restoration through Hilsa, without treating it as a universal Hilsa closure. The restricted cohort is Indian Kailash–Mansarovar pilgrims entering China from Nepal. Earlier Yari/Humla reopening for broader or different traffic is not evidence that this cohort could cross at that time. Actual pilgrimage travel is reported by 2 July 2025. Mid-March airport arrivals are not first border crossings, and a June permission announcement is not the first operational passage. Original onset and earliest restoration remain unknown; numeric duration is withheld. Human disease control is supported for the original pandemic interruption. Later geopolitical reporting is not converted into an official rationale for the whole unobserved interval. The police-attributed OnlineKhabar report was freshly read; the July Kathmandu Post report and the 2023 comparator were reread from saved passages. Police counts, traveller interviews and generic reopening accounts retain their distinct roles. The saved border-control node 2191097268 matches 30.1532053 / 81.3329027. Separate immigration-office and Hilsa police nodes support crossing identity only. Preserve one-way Nepal-to-China pilgrimage scope and dated-evidence-only display; no specific bridge, booth or queue is located.
